faqs.question: What is the difference between a Marketplace and a Merchant of Record (MoR)?
faqs.answer: A traditional digital marketplace or checkout tool (such as Gumroad) acts as an intermediary facilitating payments, but the creator remains the legal seller of record responsible for business registration, consumer rights disputes, and potentially localized indirect tax nexus filings. In contrast, a Merchant of Record (such as Lemon Squeezy) becomes the legal entity selling the product to the end consumer. The MoR assumes full legal responsibility for calculating, collecting, and remitting global sales tax, VAT, and GST in over 100 countries, protecting creators from international tax compliance liabilities.

guideContent.executiveSummary: For online course educators, academic coaches, and digital academy founders, evaluating Teachable versus Kajabi represents a classic trade-off between entry-level software subscription fees and programmatic transaction rake. Teachable offers a low upfront hurdle with its Basic plan at $59.00 per month, but penalizes educators by taking a 5% transaction commission on every single course sale in addition to standard Stripe processing fees (2.9% + $0.30). In contrast, Kajabi charges a substantially higher base SaaS subscription starting at $149.00 per month on its Basic tier, but enforces a strict 0% transaction fee across all plans. This architectural distinction creates a dramatic mathematical crossover point: once an online educator generates more than $1,800.00 in gross monthly course enrollments, Teachable's 5% transaction rake exceeds the entire $90.00 monthly subscription delta of Kajabi, making Kajabi the more profitable software host despite its higher sticker price.

workedExample.scenarioTitle: Data Analytics Academy: 60 Monthly Course Enrollments at $149.00 ($8,940.00 Gross)
workedExample.narrative: An educator launches an online data analytics certification course priced at $149.00, enrolling 60 new students each month ($8,940.00 in gross monthly tuition). On Teachable Basic ($59.00/month flat), Teachable takes a 5% transaction fee ($447.00) plus standard credit card processing of 2.9% + $0.30 per student ($277.26), incurring $783.26 in total monthly software and platform costs. On Kajabi Basic ($149.00/month flat), Kajabi takes 0% transaction fee, meaning platform costs are just the $149.00 SaaS subscription plus the identical $277.26 in credit card processing, totaling $426.26. By choosing Kajabi, the course creator saves $357.00 every single month ($4,284.00 annually) on the exact same student volume, while simultaneously unlocking Kajabi's integrated email marketing and landing page builder.

Step 2: Calculate Teachable Basic All-in Cost: $59.00 SaaS subscription + (5% platform fee * $8,940 = $447.00) + (2.9% + $0.30 gateway = $277.26) = $783.26 total monthly cost (8.76% effective cut).
Step 3: Calculate Kajabi Basic All-in Cost: $149.00 SaaS subscription + (0% platform fee = $0.00) + (2.9% + $0.30 gateway = $277.26) = $426.26 total monthly cost (4.77% effective cut).
Step 4: Determine Exact Mathematical Crossover Point: ($149 Kajabi - $59 Teachable) / 5% Teachable fee = $1,800.00 in gross monthly tuition.
Step 5: Compute Net Monthly and Annual Creator Savings with Kajabi: $783.26 (Teachable) - $426.26 (Kajabi) = $357.00 monthly cash savings ($4,284.00 annualized extra profit).

optimizationLevers.title: Graduate from Teachable Basic to Pro Once Gross Volume Exceeds $2,000
optimizationLevers.actionableAdvice: If you prefer Teachable's course player interface, never stay on the Basic plan past $2,000 in monthly sales. Upgrading to Teachable Pro ($159/mo) eliminates the 5% transaction fee entirely, saving $250+ per month on a $5,000 volume compared to remaining on Basic.

optimizationLevers.title: Consolidate External Marketing Tools into Kajabi's All-in-One Suite
optimizationLevers.actionableAdvice: Teachable focuses primarily on course hosting and student quizzes, requiring educators to purchase external tools like ConvertKit ($79/mo) and Leadpages ($49/mo). Kajabi includes native email marketing funnels, landing page builders, and CRM pipelines, saving $1,500+ annually in external SaaS subscriptions.

optimizationLevers.title: Leverage Teachable's Merchant of Record Features for Global VAT
optimizationLevers.actionableAdvice: Teachable offers a native 'BackOffice' service that acts as a Merchant of Record, automatically remitting EU VAT and distributing automated payouts to affiliate partners. Kajabi requires creators to connect personal Stripe accounts and manage localized tax compliance directly.

optimizationLevers.title: Offer Split-Payment Plans with Built-In Financing Premiums
optimizationLevers.actionableAdvice: For flagship courses priced over $500, offer a 3-month payment plan with a 15% financing markup ($195/month x 3 = $585 vs $500 lump sum). Both Teachable and Kajabi handle automated installment billing, increasing student conversion while generating additional margin.

faqs.question: At what exact sales volume does Kajabi become cheaper than Teachable?
faqs.answer: Kajabi becomes mathematically cheaper than Teachable at exactly $1,800.00 in gross monthly course sales (comparing Teachable Basic at $59/month plus 5% transaction fee against Kajabi Basic at $149/month with 0% transaction fee). Beyond $1,800 monthly volume, Teachable's 5% cut exceeds Kajabi's $90 monthly price difference, producing substantial compounding creator savings as enrollment scales.

faqs.question: Does Teachable charge a transaction fee on all of its subscription tiers?
faqs.answer: No. Teachable only assesses its 5% transaction commission on the entry-level Basic plan ($59/month). On the Pro plan ($159/month) and Pro+ plan ($279/month), Teachable eliminates the 5% transaction fee, charging 0% platform commission (subject only to standard credit card gateway processing fees of 2.9% + $0.30 across all student enrollments).

faqs.question: Can I replace email marketing software like ConvertKit with Kajabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. One of Kajabi's primary selling propositions is its comprehensive all-in-one architecture. Kajabi includes native email marketing automation, visual funnel pipelines, landing page builders, blog hosting, and CRM contact tagging, allowing creators to cancel standalone subscriptions to ConvertKit, Mailchimp, or ClickFunnels and save over ,000 to ,500 annually in external software costs.

faqs.question: How do Teachable and Kajabi handle student payment processing?
faqs.answer: Teachable offers Teachable Payments (powered by Stripe Express), allowing students to pay via credit card, PayPal, Google Pay, and Apple Pay with automated global tax handling. Kajabi connects directly to your personal Stripe and PayPal accounts via Kajabi Payments, transferring student tuition into your business bank account on a daily rolling basis.

faqs.question: Which platform is better for building interactive student communities?
faqs.answer: Kajabi features a completely redesigned, standalone Community 2.0 product (built on its acquisition of Vibely) offering mobile apps, live video meetups, challenge leaderboards, and chat channels. Teachable provides basic student discussion sidebars on lecture lessons, but lacks a full-featured community environment without integrating external platforms like Circle or Discord, increasing your monthly software stack expenses.
